name: Mass Effect
strap: Meet the crew. Find your starting point.
description: Start Mass Effect without a completionist checklist: entry points, optional DLC, character routes, and a spoiler-aware story timeline.
intro: You do not need the novels, comics, multiplayer, or every side quest. Pick the kind of adventure you want, then let the crew and the main story guide you.
recommendation: Start Mass Effect 1 in Legendary Edition for the fullest character journey. If its older combat is a barrier, Mass Effect 2 is a workable alternative. Andromeda offers a separate exploration story.
basics: Humans are still negotiating their place in a galaxy shaped by older spacefaring societies.
Mass relays connect distant regions. The Citadel is a political centre where species compete and cooperate.
Importing your save preserves many decisions across the trilogy. There is no need to chase a perfect outcome or consult a guide for every conversation.

entries.title: Mass Effect 1 in Legendary Edition
entries.audience: I want the strongest character journey
entries.why: You meet the crew before their relationships and choices accumulate. Legendary Edition collects the three main games and their major story DLC in one package.
entries.need: Humanity is new to galactic politics. Shepard is a soldier whose values and relationships you help define.
entries.skip: Novels, comics, multiplayer, exhaustive planet surveys, and a perfect-playthrough checklist.
entries.tradeoff: The first game’s combat and exploration show their age. Choose a comfortable difficulty and follow your curiosity rather than clearing every map.
entries.next: Import your save into Mass Effect 2, then Mass Effect 3. Add the suggested DLC when it fits your interests.

entries.title: Mass Effect 2
entries.audience: I want to meet the crew with more immediate action
entries.why: Recruitment and loyalty missions provide a clear structure, and the combat is easier to enter than the original game.
entries.need: Use the included Genesis recap, where available, to establish key Mass Effect 1 choices. It cannot reproduce every relationship or decision from a full save.
entries.skip: A full Mass Effect 1 playthrough if it is stopping you from beginning, plus all external media.
entries.tradeoff: You lose the experience of meeting returning characters for the first time. Some details use defaults rather than decisions from a full imported save.
entries.next: Read the ME1 recap only if you accept its spoilers, play recruitment and loyalty missions, then continue to Mass Effect 3.

entries.title: Mass Effect: Andromeda
entries.audience: I want exploration and flexible combat
entries.why: A new protagonist, crew, and galaxy provide an independent way into the setting. No trilogy save is required.
entries.need: The Initiative has travelled from the Milky Way to find new homes. You play Ryder, a Pathfinder working with explorers and settlers.
entries.skip: The entire Shepard trilogy, its DLC, novels, comics, and multiplayer.
entries.tradeoff: Its tone and structure differ from the trilogy, and it leaves some wider questions open. It is not the continuation of Shepard’s crew story.
entries.next: Play the main campaign and crew missions you enjoy. Try Mass Effect 1 later if you want the trilogy’s political and character journey.

events.title: Mass Effect
events.premise: Commander Shepard investigates a threat while humanity seeks a place among the galaxy’s established powers.
events.recap: Shepard discovers that Sovereign is a Reaper, not merely Saren’s ship. The attack on the Citadel is stopped, but the wider threat remains. The Council’s fate and several squadmates’ futures depend on your decisions.
events.why: The recommended beginning. Focus on the main missions, talk to your crew, and explore side stories that catch your interest.

events.title: Bring Down the Sky
events.premise: An asteroid threatens a human colony.
events.recap: Shepard confronts a batarian extremist plot. The resolution is a choice between immediate rescue and pursuit of the attacker.
events.why: Optional: a compact introduction to tensions between humans and batarians. It does not gate the next game.

events.title: Mass Effect 2
events.premise: Shepard assembles a specialist team to investigate the disappearance of human colonies.
events.recap: After Shepard’s death and reconstruction, Cerberus funds a mission against the Collectors. The final operation’s casualties depend on preparation, loyalty, upgrades, and assignments. Do not assume every character survives.
events.why: An alternative entry if the first game’s combat puts you off. Its recruitment and loyalty missions carry the emotional core of the game.

events.title: Lair of the Shadow Broker
events.premise: A mission with Liara follows an information network across Illium and beyond.
events.recap: Liara takes over the Shadow Broker’s network after the confrontation with its ruler. Shepard’s personal relationship with her remains player-dependent.
events.why: Recommended if Liara or the continuing crew relationships interest you. It bridges her roles between games.

events.title: Arrival
events.premise: A solo rescue mission becomes a race against an approaching threat.
events.recap: Shepard destroys a mass relay to delay the Reapers, killing the inhabitants of a batarian system. The consequences help explain Shepard’s circumstances at the beginning of Mass Effect 3.
events.why: Recommended bridge after the main Mass Effect 2 mission. A recap is sufficient if you want to move on.

events.title: Mass Effect 3
events.premise: An invasion forces Shepard to seek cooperation among peoples with long histories of conflict.
events.recap: The Reapers invade the galaxy. Shepard’s coalition and the outcomes of the krogan and quarian/geth conflicts depend on choices across the trilogy. The final resolution also branches; there is no single player outcome asserted by this guide.
events.why: Begin after Mass Effect 2 if possible. Political compromises and reunions matter more when you know the people involved.

events.title: From Ashes
events.premise: A visit to Eden Prime offers a new perspective on the galaxy’s ancient history.
events.recap: Javik, a surviving Prothean, joins the crew. His memories complicate the idealised picture of the Protheans found in earlier games.
events.why: Recommended early in Mass Effect 3 if ancient history interests you. Included with Legendary Edition.

events.title: Leviathan
events.premise: An investigation follows traces of a power linked to the galaxy’s oldest mysteries.
events.recap: The investigation reveals beings connected to the origin of the Reapers and the intelligence behind them. It adds context rather than replacing Shepard’s main campaign.
events.why: Recommended later in Mass Effect 3 for readers drawn to its cosmic mystery.

events.title: Omega
events.premise: Aria seeks Shepard’s help reclaiming a station from Cerberus.
events.recap: Aria retakes Omega. Shepard’s methods influence the people caught in the operation, without turning this into a necessary detour for the trilogy’s main plot.
events.why: Optional: a focused combat story if you enjoy Aria and Omega.

events.title: Citadel
events.premise: A shore-leave adventure gives Shepard and the crew time together away from the main campaign.
events.recap: A plot against Shepard gives way to a celebration with available friends. Who can attend depends on their survival and your progress.
events.why: Recommended near the end, before the final campaign point of no return. Save the social portion until your available crew stories are resolved.

events.title: Mass Effect: Andromeda
events.premise: Ryder leads explorers searching for viable homes in an unfamiliar galaxy.
events.recap: Ryder builds alliances with the angara while resisting the kett and investigating Remnant technology. The campaign resolves its immediate conflict but leaves wider Initiative questions open.
events.why: A separate entry for exploration and flexible combat. Shepard’s trilogy and its save files are not prerequisites.

characters.name: Commander Shepard
characters.motivation: Define a soldier’s values through leadership, conversations, and difficult choices.
characters.relationships: The Normandy crew is the centre of the story. Relationships and romances depend on the player.

updates.text: Your decisions determine who survives Virmire and the Council’s fate.
Working with Cerberus creates tensions with old allies; the final mission can have very different casualties.
Earlier choices shape alliances, reunions, and the options available in the final conflict.

characters.name: Garrus Vakarian
characters.motivation: He struggles with the limits of institutions and the appeal of taking justice into his own hands.
characters.relationships: His friendship with Shepard is built through shared work and conversations.

updates.text: His time on Omega reveals what happens when that drive operates outside official authority. Survival is not guaranteed.
If he survived, his perspective helps connect Shepard’s mission to the turian war effort.

characters.name: Tali’Zorah
characters.motivation: Her personal growth is entwined with the needs of a people living aboard a migrant fleet.
characters.relationships: Her father and the fleet shape her sense of duty; Shepard can become a trusted ally.

updates.text: Her loyalty mission asks whether family, truth, and public responsibility can be reconciled.
If present, her story converges with the quarian/geth conflict. Its outcome depends on your choices.

characters.name: Liara T’Soni
characters.motivation: Her fascination with ancient history leads her into a much less academic world.
characters.relationships: Her mother Benezia and her connection to Shepard help shape her story.

updates.text: She becomes the Shadow Broker, trading academic isolation for a vast information network.
Her research and information work become central to the coalition against the Reapers.

characters.name: Urdnot Wrex
characters.motivation: He carries the frustration of a people whose future is constrained by the genophage.
characters.relationships: His view of Shepard depends on whether trust can survive conflict.

updates.text: He can survive or die on Virmire; the guide does not assume one outcome.
If alive, his leadership changes the context of the genophage negotiations.

characters.name: Ashley Williams
characters.motivation: Family history and service shape her guarded view of interspecies politics.
characters.relationships: She serves alongside Kaidan and Shepard.

updates.text: She or Kaidan survives Virmire, depending on your decision.
If alive, rebuilding trust involves the consequences of Shepard’s association with Cerberus.

characters.name: Kaidan Alenko
characters.role: A human biotic and Alliance officer
characters.motivation: He balances discipline with the personal cost of humanity’s early biotic training.
characters.relationships: He serves alongside Ashley and Shepard.

updates.text: He or Ashley survives Virmire, depending on your decision.
If alive, his relationship with Shepard must contend with the Cerberus chapter.

characters.name: Miranda Lawson
characters.motivation: Control and competence protect her from a family history she cannot easily escape.
characters.relationships: Her younger sister Oriana is central to her personal stakes.

updates.text: Her loyalty story tests how far she will act independently of Cerberus.
Her later survival depends on circumstances and player decisions.

characters.name: Jack
characters.motivation: She wants autonomy after a life in which others treated her as a weapon.
characters.relationships: Trust with Shepard develops through actions rather than rank.

updates.text: Her loyalty mission confronts the Cerberus experiments that shaped her childhood.
If she survived, the Grissom Academy story shows a different outlet for her strength.

characters.name: Javik
characters.role: A character tied to the Prothean past
characters.motivation: He offers a personal perspective on a history the rest of the galaxy knows through ruins.
characters.relationships: His account challenges Liara’s assumptions about the Protheans.

updates.text: He is revealed as a living Prothean survivor and can join Shepard’s crew.

characters.name: Ryder
characters.motivation: Build a future for settlers while learning to lead an exploration team.
characters.relationships: SAM and the Tempest crew support the Pathfinder’s work.

updates.text: The search for homes becomes a struggle involving the angara, kett, and Remnant technology.

characters.name: Peebee
characters.motivation: Curiosity about Remnant technology pushes her toward risk and away from settled routines.
characters.relationships: Ryder and the Tempest crew provide a new set of personal ties.

characters.name: Nakmor Drack
characters.motivation: He wants the next generation to have a future worth defending.
characters.relationships: His granddaughter Kesh and the krogan settlers ground his priorities.

factions: A governing body whose established species do not automatically share humanity’s priorities.
Humanity’s principal military and political organisation in the trilogy.
Their conflict concerns displacement, synthetic life, and competing accounts of responsibility. Learn through the games before seeking a definitive verdict.
A people shaped by the genophage and by arguments over survival, leadership, and the future.
An organisation claiming to advance human interests. Treat its account of its motives as a viewpoint to question.
A settlement and exploration project. Its story belongs to Ryder’s branch rather than Shepard’s campaign.
scope: Covers the released Shepard trilogy, selected story DLC, and Andromeda. Legendary Edition is a collection of the trilogy, not a fourth story chapter. Pinnacle Station is absent from it; multiplayer and external media are optional to this route. DLC placements are editorial recommendations, not a mandatory mission order. For Mass Effect 3, story order places in-campaign DLC before the finale; a completion setting unlocks the whole game, including the selected DLC, so choose it only if those spoilers are acceptable. No single romance, survival outcome, or ending is treated as everyone’s canon.
sources: EA help for classic DLC and Genesis
